author: ABMN Staff
title: LSV Asset Management Sells 17,874 Shares of Apple (AAPL)
text:
Posted by ABMN Staff on May 18th, 2018 // No Comments
LSV Asset Management lessened its stake in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 1.1% in the 4th quarter, according to the company in its most recent Form 13F filing with the SEC. The fund owned 1,619,334 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 17,874 shares during the quarter. LSV Asset Management’s holdings in Apple were worth $274,039,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period.
Several other large investors also recently bought and sold shares of the stock. Oak Point Wealth Management acquired a new stake in Apple during the fourth quarter worth $163,000. Interactive Financial Advisors acquired a new stake in Apple during the fourth quarter worth $188,000. Delphi Private Advisors LLC increased its stake in Apple by 8,292.9% during the fourth quarter. Delphi Private Advisors LLC now owns 1,175 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $199,000 after acquiring an additional 1,161 shares during the last quarter. Financial & Investment Management Group Ltd. acquired a new stake in Apple during the fourth quarter worth $204,000. Finally, Hikari Power Ltd acquired a new stake in Apple during the third quarter worth $208,000. 60.93% of the stock is owned by hedge funds and other institutional investors. Get Apple alerts:
Several equities research analysts have issued reports on AAPL shares. Macquarie set a $188.00 target price on Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research note on Friday, January 26th. Barclays cut their target price on Apple from $170.00 to $168.00 and set an “equal weight” rating for the company in a research note on Friday, March 16th. Zacks Investment Research raised Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $197.00 target price for the company in a research note on Thursday, January 18th. Maxim Group raised their target price on Apple from $204.00 to $210.00 and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research note on Friday, February 2nd. Finally, Needham & Company LLC raised their target price on Apple to $210.00 and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research note on Friday, February 2nd. One analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, sixteen have assigned a hold rating, thirty-three have issued a buy rating and two have issued a strong buy rating to the company’s stock. The stock currently has a consensus rating of “Buy” and an average target price of $204.00. In related news, SVP Daniel J. Riccio sold 17,375 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction dated Wednesday, April 4th. The stock was sold at an average price of $169.12, for a total value of $2,938,460.00. Following the transaction, the senior vice president now owns 66,191 shares in the company, valued at approximately $11,194,221.92. The sale was disclosed in a legal filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is accessible through this hyperlink . Also, insider Philip W. Schiller sold 69,491 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction dated Tuesday, April 3rd. The shares were sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total value of $11,564,692.22. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Insiders sold a total of 214,869 shares of company stock worth $37,493,244 in the last 90 days. 0.08% of the stock is currently owned by insiders.
Shares of Apple opened at $186.99 on Friday, Marketbeat reports. The stock has a market capitalization of $954.83 billion, a P/E ratio of 18.16, a P/E/G ratio of 1.40 and a beta of 1.26. Apple has a 52-week low of $185.68 and a 52-week high of $188.37. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80, a quick ratio of 1.37 and a current ratio of 1.46.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last issued its quarterly earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, beating the Thomson Reuters’ consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. The firm had revenue of $61.14 billion for the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $60.94 billion. Apple had a return on equity of 39.97% and a net margin of 21.55%. The firm’s revenue for the quarter was up 15.6% on a year-over-year basis. During the same quarter in the previous year, the firm posted $2.10 EPS. equities research analysts forecast that Apple will post 11.43 EPS for the current fiscal year.
The business also recently declared a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, May 17th. Investors of record on Monday, May 14th were given a $0.73 dividend. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a yield of 1.56%. The ex-dividend date of this dividend was Friday, May 11th. This is a boost from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. Apple’s payout ratio is 31.70%.
Apple declared that its Board of Directors has initiated a stock buyback plan on Tuesday, May 1st that authorizes the company to repurchase $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This repurchase authorization authorizes the iPhone maker to buy up to 11.9% of its stock through open market purchases. Stock repurchase plans are generally a sign that the company’s leadership believes its stock is undervalued.
